propositions: Current per-candidate overlap judge invokes 2N calls (one per candidate per ordering) each resending the full 846-token system prefix, consuming ~5.8% more input tokens than pre-8415 baseline without reaching the 1024-token cache floor

Batched judging (N candidates in one call per ordering) reduces calls to 2*ceil(N/batch), eliminating redundant prefix copies and enabling the prefix to cross the 1024-token cache threshold via added batch-protocol documentation in the system prompt

Batch verdict demultiplexing must match candidates by label not position, with missing or unknown entries abstaining only the affected candidate to prevent cross-contamination of verdicts across the labelled list

Precision risk of batching (5/6 verdict relation shifts toward conservative, systematic vs 1-3/12 within-build noise) is measured not assumed; true-positive control shows full-confidence duplicates recover identically in both per-pair and batched builds
